links.statement: Mapped-clone sequencing and assembly generated the public human draft analysed from the October 2000 snapshot.

links.statement: Kornberg used complementary pairing in the Watson–Crick model to interpret template-directed enzymatic synthesis.

links.statement: The original φX174 genome report explicitly used the plus/minus sequence-reading method.
links.temporal_note: The method demonstration was documented by December 1974, before the 1977 genome-sequence report.

links.statement: Sanger, Nicklen and Coulson presented chain termination as a further polymerase sequencing method related to plus/minus.
links.temporal_note: Earlier plus/minus development is distinct from the later 1977 method.

links.statement: The consortium identified four-colour fluorescence detection, citing Smith et al., among the advances supporting automated reads.
links.temporal_note: The demonstrated readout predates production-scale refinements.

links.statement: The plus/minus assay requires complementary template copying because its sequence readout comes from primer-extension products.
links.temporal_note: Established copying operation precedes its later assay use.

links.statement: Prober’s system adapted dideoxy sequencing with four fluorescent terminators and a combined reaction/readout.
links.temporal_note: The 1977 termination publication preceded the 1987 modified-system report; these publication dates are not exact dates of the experiments.

elec-oxide-surface-stabilization-1958--c.statement: Atalla reported oxide surface stabilization at a 1958 Electrochemical Society meeting.

scope.configuration: Atalla, Tannenbaum and Scheibner measured thermally oxidized silicon interfaces and device behavior, finding stable surface potentials with characteristic interface states.

elec-oxide-surface-stabilization-1958--c.uncertainty: Meeting presentation is documented retrospectively; source does not support universal efficacy or precise later uptake date.

date.basis: Date of this documented community-facing use, recognition, or communication; not a claim of first occurrence.

elec-photolithographic-windows-1955--com.statement: Andrus issued patent publicly described photoresist-patterned windows in silicon oxide for selective diffusion.

scope.configuration: Jules Andrus and Walter Bond adapted photoresist patterning to etch windows in silicon oxide before localized diffusion.

elec-photolithographic-windows-1955--com.uncertainty: A 1958 book chapter is cited by CHM but its text has not been inspected; patent is a later awareness bound.

elec-point-contact-amplifier-1947--commu.date_basis: Date of this documented community-facing use, recognition, or communication; not a claim of first occurrence.

date.basis: Date of this documented community-facing use, recognition, or communication; not a claim of first occurrence.

elec-point-contact-amplifier-1947--commu.statement: Bell publicly announced its point-contact transistor on 30 June 1948.

scope.configuration: Bardeen and Brattain placed two closely spaced gold contacts against germanium to obtain amplification.

elec-point-contact-amplifier-1947--commu.uncertainty: Later commercial point-contact transistors are related designs; exact gold-contact original specimen transfer is not established.

elec-volta-batteries-1800--community-ent.date_basis: Date of this documented community-facing use, recognition, or communication; not a claim of first occurrence.

date.basis: Date of this documented community-facing use, recognition, or communication; not a claim of first occurrence.

elec-volta-batteries-1800--community-ent.statement: Nicholson and Carlisle used a reproduced Volta pile in water-decomposition experiments in 1800.

scope.configuration: A pile of alternating silver and zinc plates with brine-wetted pasteboard separators; the separately described chain of liquid-filled cups is not claimed as the apparatus used in the London experiments.

elec-volta-batteries-1800--community-ent.uncertainty: The independent use is established for the stacked-pile arrangement; it does not establish use of the separate cups configuration or any first offer for sale.

elec-hoerni-planar-transistor-1959--comm.date_basis: Latest documented community-use or recognition bound; no earliest date is established.

date.label: by 1960-04
date.basis: Latest documented community-use or recognition bound; no earliest date is established.

elec-hoerni-planar-transistor-1959--comm.statement: Fairchild had sold the 2N1613, a planar silicon transistor of this general configuration, by April 1960.

scope.configuration: Fairchild 2N1613 NPN silicon planar transistor, an instance of the retained-oxide configuration; the unnamed March 1959 prototype is a separate witness.

elec-hoerni-planar-transistor-1959--comm.uncertainty: The 1959 specimen’s polarity and identity are unproved; an April 1960 product sale does not establish the first commercial availability of the entire configuration class.

elec-fairchild-junction-isolation-1960--.date_basis: Latest documented community-use or recognition bound; no earliest date is established.

date.label: by 1960-11-01
date.basis: Latest documented community-use or recognition bound; no earliest date is established.

elec-fairchild-junction-isolation-1960--.statement: Fairchild R&D engineer James Nall favorably assessed electrical isolation for Micrologic by 1 November 1960, following the reported diffused-isolation flip-flops.

scope.configuration: Fairchild Micrologic electrical isolation of semiconductor circuit regions, with working boron-diffused junction-isolated flip-flops reported in the same development chronology.

elec-fairchild-junction-isolation-1960--.uncertainty: Nall evaluates electrical isolation in general; the quoted report excerpt does not identify the exact flip-flop specimen. Its association with the diffused approach is drawn from the participant chronology. The 1961 Type F die has not been identified as this specimen.

elec-photolithographic-windows-1955--fai.date_basis: Latest documented community-use or recognition bound; no earliest date is established.

date.label: by 1958
date.basis: Latest documented community-use or recognition bound; no earliest date is established.

elec-photolithographic-windows-1955--fai.statement: Fairchild used photolithographic oxide-window fabrication in its mesa transistor work and shipped 100 2N696 transistors by 1958.

scope.configuration: Fairchild’s photoresist-patterned silicon-oxide openings used to delimit diffusion in mesa transistor fabrication; individual masks need not be identical to the earlier Bell Labs masks.

elec-photolithographic-windows-1955--fai.uncertainty: The Fairchild method is contextual evidence of use of the same general patterned oxide-window process; the source does not identify every original Bell mask or prove exact transfer of a physical tool.
